anti_patterns: Treating unconfirmed roots as final: executing destination effects before the challenge window elapses collapses the pattern into a trusted-relayer bridge

Initializing a replica with a zero committed root that the adjudicator treats as confirmed: the Nomad August 2022 exploit showed confirmAt[0x00]=1 let any unproven message pass acceptableRoot and drain $190M
Relying on watchers to catch contract bugs: Nomad watchers monitored updater signatures only, so the process-function bug never triggered a fraud report
Single updater with no rotation plan: a compromised or faulty updater key halts or corrupts every replica it feeds until governance intervenes
Letting a malicious watcher grief liveness unchecked: permissioned watchers that can disconnect replicas need per-application enrollment and removal governance
Sizing bonds below profit-from-corruption: if forging a root pays more than the slashed stake, the challenge game is theater
avoid_when: Sub-second or synchronous cross-chain UX is required: the challenge window imposes a hard latency floor no tuning removes
The destination chain cannot resist censorship for the full window: a censorable destination lets an attacker finalize a forged root
No party can be relied on to watch: without at least one live watcher holding source-chain data, fraud finalizes unchallenged
Exact instant finality with strong consistency is required across chains
The team cannot staff watcher operations and fraud-recovery governance (updater rotation, replica repair, re-enrollment)
benefits: Minimal happy-path gas: no per-message header or proof verification on destination, only one storage write per batched root update plus amortized finalization
Simple destination logic: the replica replays signed roots and checks Merkle inclusion, far less code than an on-chain light client or ZK verifier
Cheap multi-destination fan-out: one home broadcast serves any number of replicas with no per-chain verification bespoke logic
Fast fraud detection: equivalence of the posted root against canonical source state is a hash comparison, so off-chain watchers detect fraud in seconds
Short windows are viable: because source data is fully available, Nomad ran a 30-minute window versus roughly 7 days for optimistic rollups
Permissionless fraud proof on origin: anyone can slash a fraudulent updater on the home contract, not only an allowlisted set
best_practices: Size the window as max(origin uncensorable period, destination uncensorable period) plus a watcher observation buffer, and re-measure per chain pair
Set updater and challenger bonds above the maximum profit-from-forgery of a single window, and re-price as bridged value grows
Run redundant watcher setups per operator key across independent infrastructure so one outage never blinds the channel
Give each application its own watcher set via a connection-manager style registry so one compromised watcher cannot halt every app
Test the zero-value edge explicitly: uninitialized mapping slots must never satisfy the accepted-root predicate
Drill the fraud-recovery runbook (unseat updater, erase fraudulent roots from every replica, rotate keys, re-enroll) before value at risk grows
Emit root-posted, challenged, and finalized events so watchers and indexers react to state transitions rather than polling
component_types: Home Contract: source-chain broadcast channel holding the canonical message tree, updater stake, and the queue of signed roots
Replica Contract: destination-chain inbox tracking posted roots with confirmAt timestamps and enforcing the optimistic timeout before message processing
Updater (Proposer): bonded off-chain agent signing root attestations from source to each replica; the only actor that can commit fraud
Watcher (Challenger): monitoring agent comparing posted roots against canonical source state and submitting fraud transactions within the window
Relayer: trustless permissionless courier ferrying signed updates and Merkle proofs between chains; needs no bond
Processor: trustless party proving message inclusion against a finalized root and invoking the destination handler
Adjudication Logic: deterministic on-chain fraud check on the home contract (slashable) plus replica disconnect on the destination side
Connection Manager: per-application registry mapping watcher addresses to replica permissions for app-governed roots of trust
context: Two sovereign blockchains need to move assets or general messages between them, but per-message verification on the destination (light-client header checks or ZK proof verification) is too expensive for the traffic volume. An optimistic bridge posts a bonded relayer's claimed source-state root to the destination contract and accepts it as valid after a fixed challenge window unless a watcher proves fraud on chain. Security rests on at least one honest watcher with source-chain data access and on the destination chain resisting censorship for the whole window. The canonical production instance is Nomad (optics v2): a Home contract on the origin broadcasts signed Merkle roots to Replica contracts on destinations with a 30-minute optimistic window.
design_principles: Assume valid, verify on dispute: pay verification cost only when challenged, never on the happy path
One honest watcher suffices: design detection so a single live monitor with data access protects the whole channel
Finalize then execute: no destination effect may run against a root whose window has not elapsed
Fraud must be cheap to detect and expensive to commit: hash-equivalence checks off chain, slashed bonds on chain
App-governed trust: each application chooses its own watcher set rather than inheriting a monolithic bridge committee
Recoverability by construction: updater rotation, fraudulent-root erasure, and replica re-enrollment are first-class flows, not afterthoughts

UMA Optimistic Oracle V3 (assertTruth, disputeAssertion, settleAssertion) for the oracle analogue
Across / UMA-based intent bridges using optimistic settlement
Generic EVM destination contracts with Merkle inclusion proving (prove/process pattern)
Off-chain watcher and relayer agents with funded hot keys per watched chain
tradeoffs: Delayed finality: every message waits out the full challenge window (Nomad: 30 minutes), so the pattern can never serve instant UX without a separate fast-liquidity layer
One-of-N watcher trust: safety collapses if all watchers go offline or lack source data during a window
Censorship assumption: an adversary able to censor the destination chain longer than the window finalizes forged roots
Challenge griefing: a malicious watcher can disconnect replicas and stall honest messages until governance removes it
Catastrophic contract-bug surface: the August 2022 Nomad exploit bypassed the challenge game entirely through a Replica initialization bug ($190M drained)
Bond economics overhead: updater and challenger capital lock-up plus watcher operating cost offset part of the gas savings
use_cases: EVM-to-EVM token bridging where per-message light-client verification would dominate cost (Nomad Home/Replica BridgeRouter flow)
General cross-chain message passing (governance votes, contract calls) to many destinations from one source broadcast
Low-frequency high-value transfers where a 30-minute settlement delay is acceptable and gas savings compound
Bootstrapping new chain connections quickly: deploying a Replica is far cheaper than building a bespoke light client per chain pair
Oracle-style data assertion with bonded dispute, as in UMA Optimistic Oracle integrations
